assumptions: all words of length <= 11 (<= 8 for the four doubling rules)
meta.falsification: H-C04-1: a bordered rule with random descent or an unbordered one without. H-C04-2: disagreement between observed random descent and the critical-peak test.
meta.hypothesis: H-C04-1 (bold): a terminating one-rule system has random descent iff its left-hand side is unbordered. H-C04-2: a terminating one-rule system has random descent iff each of its critical peaks (r s <- p b s -> p r for l = p b = b s) is joinable by two derivations of EQUAL length.
meta.methodology: Exact min/max derivation lengths and the set of reachable normal forms per word from the derivation graph; random descent = all maximal derivations from each word have the same length AND the same normal form (van Oostrom); critical peaks joined by breadth-first search over exact step counts.
meta.question: When do all maximal derivations from every word have the same length (random descent)?
meta.title: Random descent of one-rule systems: unbordered left-hand sides versus critical peaks

summary: H-C04-1 counterexamples: 18 (e.g. [['aa', ''], ['aa', 'a'], ['aa', 'aba'], ['bb', '']]); unbordered rules without RD: 0
H-C04-2 disagreements (RD vs equal-length joinable critical peaks): 0; length-uniform but not confluent: 0
